question.text: The 'settlor' in an AIF trust structure is typically:

answer.text: The custodian who holds the fund's assets
The person or entity that creates the trust by transferring property/assets to it
The investor who contributes the largest amount
SEBI which approves the fund's registration

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.188-189) explains that an AIF trust is established by a trust indenture (trust deed) executed between the settlor and the trustee. The settlor is the author of the trust who settles the trust and conveys an initial sum to the trustee to create the trust assets. In the AIF context the sponsor may act as the settlor (p.189), while the manager's role and responsibilities are described separately (p.45). The Trap: The custodian merely holds assets for safekeeping, the largest investor remains a beneficiary, and SEBI is the regulator — none of these create the trust by settling its initial property. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.188-189 (settlor/trustee/trust indenture; settlor conveys initial sum; sponsor may act as settlor) and p.45 (manager role).
